title: A task is not done while its feature needs a switch turned on by hand
goal: For five days the loop built about twenty video features, audited them and called them ready to try, while every one sat behind a switch that is off by default, so the user opening a recording saw none of it. The rule now says a feature must be reachable at Next defaults; make the queue check it when a task is marked done, instead of trusting each runner to remember.
notes: Evidence, checked 2026-09-23 by the digest pass: Sources/PhotonzCore/FeatureCatalog.swift, the recordingIsADocumentFlag entry (next-a-recording-is-a-document) has enabledByDefaultIn: [] while the video features under it (next-sound-on-the-timeline, next-open-out-the-timeline, next-hear-the-scrub, next-export-the-video and more) are enabledByDefaultIn: [.next]. The 2026-09-22 digest told the user video cutting was genuinely tryable end to end. runner-prompt.md now says it in prose (Default config, section around line 308); prose was not enough last time. The fix for the flag itself is a-recording-opens-in-the-video-editor-for-real-i; this task is the gate so the next parent switch cannot hide a feature the same way. Walk setups carry flags in their JSON (see a-walk-can-switch-a-feature-off-before-it-runs, done).
acceptance: Marking an app task done is refused, with a sentence saying which switch, when none of the walks it names reaches the feature without turning a switch on by hand, unless the task says in so many words that it is deliberately off by default
The check reads the switch's real default for Next from the app's own list of switches, not from what the audit claims
An audit records which switches its setup changed from the Next defaults, and the dashboard shows an audit that changed any as not reachable yet
A test feeds the check a task whose only walk switches on a feature that is off by default and sees it refused

log.note: Manager pass 2026-09-23 07:44: half of this landed with 71b217f7 (A recording opens in the video editor at Next defaults). FeatureCatalog now records what a flag needs, and Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/FeatureDependencyTests.swift fails when a flag on by default in Next needs one that is off. Build the done-check on that list rather than a second one; what is still missing is the queue side: refusing done when the task's walks force a flag on, and the audit recording which switches its setup changed.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Built: queue/bin/flag-defaults.mjs reads each switch's default straight from FeatureCatalog.swift; queue.mjs status <id> done (runner path only; the dashboard and sweep-report are not gated) refuses an app task when every walk it names switches ON something off at the release's defaults, naming walk and switch, unless queue.mjs off-by-default <id> "<why>" says so. Audits carry switched:{...}; auditIndex judges it against the catalog and the Ready to try card and report show Not reachable yet. FlagDefaultsReaderTests holds the reader to the catalog and runs queue/bin/reach-drill.mjs (22 checks) inside Scripts/test.sh. Checked against the real queue: no open or done task naming walks would be refused today; a-separation-arrives-shut-walk alone would be.

left rough: an app task that names no walks is not judged at all, so a runner can skip the gate by not naming any. Making walks mandatory would refuse every non-UI app task; the runner prompt now tells UI tasks to name theirs. Did not earn a task: file it if a feature slips through that way. No audit written: this is loop infrastructure, and the one visible change (the Not reachable yet label) was checked on a sandbox dashboard on port 8799 with a forced and a plain audit.

Shipped in 14c10691: done on an app task is refused when every walk it names switches on something off at Next defaults (read from FeatureCatalog.swift via queue/bin/flag-defaults.mjs), with an off-by-default escape in words; audits record switched and the dashboard shows Not reachable yet. Verified by FlagDefaultsReaderTests + reach-drill (22 checks) in a green Scripts/test.sh (10,141 tests), and on a sandbox dashboard.
